raw_recipe.headline: Tuna Fish Salad
raw_recipe.description: Easy tuna fish salad flavored with parsley, garlic, and lemon mixed with canned tuna, celery, onion, and mayonnaise great in sandwiches and on salads.
raw_recipe.name: Tuna Fish Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Combine tuna, mayonnaise, celery, onion, parsley, lemon juice, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl; mix well. Season with paprika; refrigerate until chilled.

review.reviewBody: I have been making this tuna salad since it was uploaded over 4 years ago. Definitely only make this with 12 oz of tuna. Do NOT be afraid to add more celery and onion. In mine I put closer to 1/2 cup of each. Also, in addition to everything in this recipe try adding 3/4 TBSP of red wine vinegar. It is AMAZING. I just made a batch and I think I would ruin it by putting in on a sandwich with cheese. For now I'm just eating it with crackers so I can taste all of the fresh flavors.

So I made this recipe twice to figure out things. First, note the size of the tuna can used 5oz. In another recipe I made the mistake of assuming that they are all same size and ended up with too much mayo for the amount of tuna. Even still, for me half a cup of mayonnaise is too much and I went for 4.5 tablespoons. I like my salad to be a tuna salad with mayo not a mayo salad with tuna. I used Hellmann's Real Mayo which I feel has a strong flavor compared to other brands. I liked the freshness of this recipe with the fresh chopped ingredients added like celery, onion and parsley. I compared this to Barbie's Tuna Salad which is the highest rated on allrecipes and this surely tastes fresher, but in terms of flavor punch Barbie has got it. Make sure you drain your tuna well even if you have to use a strainer. Extra water will affect the texture of the salad and make it mushy. The texture is quite chunky with almost every bite got the crunch of celery and onion. You may want to reduce the amounts a bit. Also try to go for red onion which is milder than white. I went with white onion at the first trial and it was too oniony. My next trial I used only 2 tablespoons of white onion and it balanced out. Make sure you dice celery onion into small pieces so that it spreads out evenly in the mixture.

I love this recipe. I doubled the recipe and added 3 chopped hard boiled eggs. I minced the white onion amount to my taste. I think that tuna fish in oil tastes better than tuna in water and I chopped my celery a little finer. Everyone in the family loves my Tuna salad.

I make it at least once a week, to take a break from other meats. Left out celery this time. Only had dried parsley on hand. Added 3 large boiled eggs. Extra white onions, added pickle relish and a teaspoon of sugar because we were out of sweet relish. Sprinkled paprika on top before putting in fridge. YUM!! Helamans mayo. Oh, served with fresh baguettes from Continental Bakery. Near me
Easy, Easy ingredients. Hubby approved. I used slightly less than the 1/2 cup mayo to the 1 can of tuna and it was wet enough for our tastes.

I changed it up a little to suit my taste. I used 2 cans of tuna. 1/3 cup of mayo. 1/4 c of sweet relish. 2 tbl of minced onions. 1 celery stalk or 1/2 c of minced green pepper. 1 tb of lemon juice. 1/2 tb of dried parsley. 1/2 tsp of garlic powder. 1/2 tsp of salt. 1/4 tsp of black pepper. Yum!

It is worth doubling the recipe. I made a few changes using 1/2 T of red wine vinegar, and I used Greek yogurt for half of the mayo and I used a combo of light mayo and ranch for the rest. I took out the salt (since ranch is salty) and I used more celery. I also added a hint of yellow mustard because I love it. It was great and my husband approved (and he is a picky eater).

I would give five stars but the tuna to mayo ratio is off in my opinion - 3 cans of tuna rather than the 1 can the recipe calls for fits with the 1/2 c. of mayo called for. I only used a shake of the salt and pepper too. All else I did according to the recipe, and might I say DElicious! I liked the addition of lemon juice - really sets off the tuna flavor so it doesn't get lost with the other ingredients. A wonderful switch off from the old tuna/mayo/pickles recipe. EDIT: I also use red onion instead of yellow for additional flavor. I discovered this works really well atop a plain Pretzel Crisp too!

I initially tried this with one small 5 oz can of tuna, and it was way too much mayo. I simply added another can, and it was perfect. You could probably use 3 cans if you want to cut down on the mayo further. I used white albacore in water and Hellman's low fat mayo. I found it tasted even better after letting it refrigerate overnight!
Doubled the recipe and added 1/2 tablespoon sweet relish

Great recipe, but I prefer to use primal kitchen mayo which has avacado oil instead of the other mayo's that use fattening seed oils. And I use safe catch tuna fish, sold at fresh market, it says it has less mercury. Again, thanks for the awesome ingredient list!
Made as stated. Not my childhood tunafish salad. I’ll keep looking for the right recipe.

Really good recipe! Not too hard to make either. I definitely recommend adding in some diced pickled jalapenos for an extra kick. A splash of the vinegar juice also. Everyone in my family seems to like it. Definitely worth a try. 💪👍

I had a 12 oz can of Albacore so I doubled the ingredients to equal 10 oz can, because math. I think that at a full cup of mayo was much too thin. I believe next time I'll go with between a half and 3/4 of a cup I guess I just like mine firmer is what I'm trying to say. Regardless of that I thought it was very good and I thank you for taking the time to put this on the internet for people to find
May add some things like grapes and nuts but otherwise great base recipe!
Thanks alot
I add sweet relish to taste or about two tablespoons. My husband and I love this recipe.
Just half the amount of mayo. Other than that, it was a hit and will do this recipe as my go to

I always add a snap of mustard. Regular or dijon. Mustard is a must, along with a squirt of lemon. Sometimes I cheat and use salad dressing... added to or instead of mayo... your choice, blue cheese or creamy caesar. I think adding paprika puts it into a different bend in the river... but its still legitimate. Different strokes.
😋 yummy
